jsonld.name: Cornish Hog's Pudding Breakfast
jsonld.description: The West Country's answer to black pudding: hog's pudding — a coarse, pale sausage of pork, suet, and bread, seasoned with pepper, mace, and sometimes leek — sliced thick and fried to a golden crust that gives way to a soft, savoury, faintly peppery middle. It is breakfast meat at its most old-fashioned and least apologetic, and on the Cornish plate it takes the black pudding's slot: beside the egg, under the sauce, with the tomato's sharpness standing against its richness. The technique is the gentle sear: hog's pudding is softer than black pudding and wants a lower, slower fry to crust the faces without the middle collapsing into the pan. Six minutes, two turns, one egg's worth of patience.

Cornish Hog's Pudding Breakfast

British · Easy · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The West Country's answer to black pudding: hog's pudding — a coarse, pale sausage of pork, suet, and bread, seasoned with pepper, mace, and sometimes leek — sliced thick and fried to a golden crust that gives way to a soft, savoury, faintly peppery middle. It is breakfast meat at its most old-fashioned and least apologetic, and on the Cornish plate it takes the black pudding's slot: beside the egg, under the sauce, with the tomato's sharpness standing against its richness. The technique is the gentle sear: hog's pudding is softer than black pudding and wants a lower, slower fry to crust the faces without the middle collapsing into the pan. Six minutes, two turns, one egg's worth of patience.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The hog's pudding

The plate

Seasoning

  • the pudding seasons)
- **Source it properly:** hog's pudding is a Cornish butcher's item — a real one is coarse, pale, and loosely packed. If the West Country is nowhere near, a good butchers' white pudding (its Irish cousin) cooks identically and reads the same on the plate. - **Cut thick and chill:** 2 cm slices from a cold coil hold their shape; thin slices or a warm coil slump at the crust stage. Keep everything fridge-cold until the pan is ready. - The plate builds café-style: pudding, eggs, tomato, mushrooms, toast — hog's pudding replaces black pudding and behaves with the same sequencing.

Cornish Hog's Pudding Breakfast

Prep: 5 minutes · Cook: 20 minutes · Total: 25 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The hog's pudding

  • 1 hog's pudding coil or 6 thick slices (300 g), cut 2 cm thick if slicing yourself

The plate

  • 4 large eggs (220 g)
  • 15 g butter
  • 2 medium vine tomatoes (250 g), halved and grilled
  • 150 g chestnut mushrooms, halved, browned
  • 2 slices (140 g) thick toast or fried bread

Seasoning

  • 10 ml / 10 g neutral oil
  • 2 g fine sea salt (light — the pudding seasons)
  • 1 g black pepper
  • Brown breakfast sauce

Instructions

  1. **The gentle sear, 8–9 minutes.** Film the pan with the oil over medium-low heat. Lay in the slices and cook 4 minutes undisturbed to a deep gold crust, then turn carefully — a fish slice fully slid under, one motion — and give 3–4 minutes more. The second side cooks faster; watch it. Checkpoint — both faces crusted deep gold, the slices holding their shape with edges just beginning to round, and the middles warmed through — a probe reads 65 °C-plus, though the eye is enough: the slice gives gently under a fingertip, springy-soft, not molten. This is the doneness line; hog's pudding has no raw state to fear, only a collapsed one.
  2. **The plate's supports, in the same pan.** Mushrooms in the residual fat for 4 minutes to browned; tomatoes grilled alongside from the start. Checkpoint — mushrooms glossed brown; tomatoes slumped jammy — the plate's acid note standing ready against the pudding's richness.
  3. **The eggs, last, 3 minutes.** Butter into the pan, eggs in when it foams, basted to the butter-basted master's spec — set whites, lace edges, running yolks. Checkpoint — whites set, yolks running, the eggs cooked in the pudding's lightly peppered fat — the plate's signature seasoning, done by the pan.
  4. **Plate and sauce.** Pudding slices centred, eggs at the crown, tomato and mushrooms flanking, toast beneath. Brown sauce over the pudding — its fruit-sharpness is the traditional partner to hog's pudding's pepper — and tea alongside. Checkpoint — the eating test: crust, then the soft peppered middle, then the tomato's acid resetting — the West Country plate complete, and no black pudding mourned.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Slices collapsed to crumbHeat too high or slices thinMedium-low, 2 cm, cold slices
Greasy plateSuet rendered out fullyThe gentle sear holds the fat in; pull at gold, not bronze
Bland puddingIndustrial-soft recipeA proper butcher's coarse pudding; the pepper should announce itself

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **A raw coil keeps 5 days refrigerated** and freezes 3 months; cooked slices keep 3 days and re-crust gently in 2 minutes a side. - **Variation — the full Cornish plate:** add a sautéed potato cake and a mug of clotted-cream-less builder's tea — the county's breakfast, rendered honestly. - **Variation — the hog's pudding bap:** slices in a buttered bap with the café-style fried onions and brown sauce — the West Country's sausage sarnie, upgraded. - **The pudding family:** black (blood and oat, the pan's boldest), white (the Irish cousin,closest in texture), and hog's (the Cornish suet-soft) — three records, one slot on the plate, each with its own frying law.

methodSteps.chefsNote: hog's pudding's softness is its character and its hazard: cooked hot, the suet runs out and the slice disintegrates into crumb; cooked at medium-low, the crust forms before the middle softens and the slice keeps its architecture. The test is the turn — if a slice needs coaxing, it is not crusted yet; give it a minute. The same law runs the black pudding master at higher confidence, because black pudding's oat body is sturdier. This one asks for the gentler hand.
